title: Human Excretory System
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Diagrams of the skin layers and the urinary system; a sheep's kidney from the butcher cut by the teacher if possible. Link each organ to the waste it removes. Health statements are to be confirmed by a teacher or a health worker.

skills.key_step: The child names the organs of excretion and the waste each removes: kidneys (urea, excess water and salts in urine), lungs (carbon dioxide and water vapour), skin (sweat: water, salts, some urea), liver (breaks down wastes), and knows faeces are not excretion.

floor.prerequisite: Knows what the lungs give out.
floor.question: Which gas do we breathe out more of?

representations: a body outline with the organs
steps: Excretion removes waste made by the body's cells.
Kidneys: urine. Lungs: carbon dioxide. Skin: sweat.
Faeces are undigested food: egestion, not excretion.

board.do: Draw a body with kidneys, lungs and skin.

board.say: Which waste do the lungs remove?

board.do: Ask the child to write the waste for each organ.

misconceptions.ask: Was the food in faeces ever used by the cells?
misconceptions.repair: Faeces are undigested food, not excreted waste.

misconceptions.ask: What do the lungs give out?

misconceptions.repair: Sweat also removes water and salts.

misconceptions.ask: Which organ breaks down old red cells?

checks.question: Which organ removes urea in urine?

skills.key_step: The child names the parts of the skin (epidermis, dermis, sweat gland, sweat pore, hair follicle, blood vessels, fat layer) and what each does.

floor.question: What does the skin give out?

representations: a diagram of the skin cut through
a hand lens on the back of the hand
steps: Dermis: holds sweat glands, hair follicles and blood vessels.
Sweat gland makes sweat; it leaves through a pore.
Fat layer below keeps heat in.
contexts: goose bumps on a cold morning

board.do: Draw the skin as two layers with a coiled gland in the lower one.
Ask the child to draw the tube to the pore.

misconceptions.ask: Which layer holds the sweat gland?
misconceptions.repair: Sweat glands are in the dermis.

misconceptions.ask: Does blood come out of a pore?
misconceptions.repair: A pore is the opening of a sweat duct.

listen_for: hair grows from the top layer
misconceptions.repair: Hair grows from follicles in the dermis.

misconceptions.ask: How many layers did the diagram show?

checks.question: Name the two main layers of the skin.
Where is sweat made?
checks.answer: in the sweat gland in the dermis

skills.key_step: The child names the parts of the urinary system (two kidneys, ureters, bladder, urethra) in the order urine passes and says what each does.
representations: a diagram of the urinary system
steps: Kidneys filter the blood and make urine.
Ureters carry urine to the bladder.
The urethra carries urine out of the body.
contexts: drinking water on a hot day

board.do: Draw two kidneys, two tubes to a bag, one tube out.
Point at the tubes from the kidneys.
Label the bladder and the urethra.

misconceptions.ask: Which part stores urine until we go to the toilet?

listen_for: a drink goes straight to the bladder
misconceptions.ask: What carries the water from the gut to the kidneys?
misconceptions.repair: Water goes into the blood first; the kidneys filter it.

listen_for: the urethra comes from the kidney
misconceptions.ask: Which tube joins the kidney to the bladder?
misconceptions.repair: Ureters come from the kidneys; the urethra leaves the bladder.

misconceptions.ask: How many kidneys did the diagram show?

checks.question: Which tube carries urine from a kidney to the bladder?
Put in order: bladder, kidney, urethra, ureter.

skills.key_step: The child says what causes common kidney disorders (too little water, too much salt, misuse of painkillers, untreated infections, high blood pressure) and which habits protect the kidneys and the skin (drink water, less salt, medicines as advised, daily washing, sun protection).

floor.prerequisite: Can name the parts of the urinary system.
floor.question: Which part stores urine?

representations: a chart: habit, protects kidneys or skin
steps: Wash the skin daily and treat cuts; see a health worker for pain when urinating.
contexts: a hot day at the school field
a farmer working in the sun

board.do: Write "kidney stones" and draw an arrow from "too little water".

board.say: Why does too little water help stones form?

board.do: Ask the child to add two habits that protect the kidneys.

misconceptions.ask: Are kidney stones caused by germs from another person?
misconceptions.repair: Kidney disorders are not caught from others.

misconceptions.ask: What does more water do to urine?
misconceptions.repair: Drinking enough water protects the kidneys.

misconceptions.ask: What builds up on skin each day?

checks.question: Give one habit that protects the kidneys.
checks.answer: drink enough water, eat less salt, take medicines as advised

checks.question: Give one habit that keeps the skin healthy.
checks.answer: wash daily, treat cuts, protect from strong sun
